items.text:
Sol.126.(b) They supply mineral-rich fluids that support chemosynthetic life
Hydrothermal  vents  release  mineral-laden  fluids  that  sustain bacteria  using  chemical  reactions  to  produce  energy,  forming the foundation of the deep-sea food chain.
Sol.127.(a) Life cannot exist without sunlight
The  discovery  of  vent  ecosystems showed that organisms can survive  using  chemical  energy  instead  of  sunlight,  challenging the earlier belief that sunlight was essential for all life.
Sol.128.(b) It threatens to destroy delicate and ancient ecosystems
The    passage   warns   that    mining     for minerals   like   cobalt and   nickel    may irreversibly harm fragile habitats that evolved over thousands of years.
Sol.129.(c) Producing food through chemical reactions Chemosynthetic refers to organisms that synthesise food using energy derived from chemical processes rather than sunlight, as occurs near hydrothermal vents.
Sol.130.(c) The abyssal plain hosts unique ecosystems that rely on chemical  energy and need protection
The  passage  emphasises that life in the abyssal plain depends on chemical energy from hydrothermal vents and warns against the damage  caused  by  deep-sea  mining,  highlighting  both uniqueness and the need for preservation.
